chunks: Some of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Ḥakam al-Khayyāṭ, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'Can a son recompense his father?' He said, 'No, except in two cases: if he finds him enslaved, he buys him and emancipates him; or if he has a debt, he pays it off on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: How can a son repay or recompense his father according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific mechanisms for a son to discharge his father's obligations are limited to emancipation from slavery or settling financial debts, highlighting the tangible nature of filial duty in Shia jurisprudence. This excludes general spiritual merit or prayer, emphasizing that 'recompense' here refers to the settlement of specific worldly liabilities or status changes. The hadith underscores the practical responsibility of children to alleviate their parents' burdens, a key theme in the ethics of family relations (birr al-walidayn).

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 23.One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Ḥakam al-Khayyāṭ, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said to him, “Can a son recompense his father?”
He said, “No, except in two cases: he finds him enslaved so he buys him and emancipates him, or he is indebted so he pays off his debt.”
